Xiaomi's Winged SU7 Ultra Prototype Is Back on Track With No Camo Whatsoever
27 photos
Photo: Baldauf
Referred to as either SU7 Ultra Extreme or SU7 Ultra with the Track Package, whatever Xiaomi may be developing at the Nurburgring Nordschleife is certainly going to challenge Porsche's record lap time. Spotted with no camouflage whatsoever, the most track-focused iteration of the full-electric sedan from China displays a ginormous swan neck-style rear wing.
A redesigned front bumper, serious aerodynamic enhancements down the sides, and carbon-fiber componentry are on the menu as well, along with a redesigned aerodynamic diffuser that appears inspired by the world of motorsports. All told, Xiaomi appears to be developing the SU7 Ultra in three directions.
First and foremost, chassis enhancements are critical to lapping the Green Hell faster than the Taycan Turbo GT modified in collaboration with Manthey. Then there's the balance between downforce and aerodynamic efficiency, which needs to be perfectly so in order for this variant of the SU7 Ultra to make sense on public roads as well. The final piece of the puzzle comes in the form of weight savings. And yes, unsprung weight savings are likely as well.
A closer look at the yellow prototype reveals a more prominent front splitter with larger intakes in the bumper, along with two openings in the hood. Those are dual air ducts, and the air they shoot upward creates downforce over the front axle for improved stability when taking a corner at high speed.
The lower section of the front bumper also channels air to the sides, around the front wheels, and Xiaomi also made a case for wheel arch-mounted extractors that would make the 911 GT3 RS blush in awe. Those openings are designed to release high-pressure air trapped inside the front wheel wells, further reducing lift while improving airflow around the front axle.
Photo: Baldauf Look even closer, and you will notice front fenders that curve inward ahead of the front doors. The rear quarters feature cutaways behind the wheels as well, and the side skirts sure mean business. The distinctly motorsport-inspired appearance is topped by the dual-element rear wing.
Impossible to miss, this piece of hardware sits high enough to operate in relatively clean air. The lower section of the wing adds another surface for generating aerodynamic load. Regarding the swan-neck construction, the pylons may hide electric actuators for a drag reduction system.
DRS would be of great help on long straightaways, where less downforce equals higher speeds. The movable section could also change its angle by itself, depending on the drive mode, the governing software, and what the sensors are transmitting to the system's control unit.
Equipped with double-spoke wheels, beefy front and rear brakes, and a carbon-fiber roof that includes a front-facing lidar sensor, the prototype in these photos also features body-hugging bucket seats with a Nurburgring motif on the seatbacks. This alone indicates that Xiaomi wants to dethrone the Manthey-prepped Porsche Taycan Turbo GT at the 'Ring, besting the SU7 Ultra Track Package's previous 7:04 lap time.
The Porker required 6 minutes and 55 seconds with Lars Kern behind the wheel. Vincent Radermecker remains Xiaomi's go-to specialist for Green Hell shenanigans. Including the SU7 Ultra Track Package, the Belgian racing driver broke the four-door sedan record a couple of times with Jaguar's XE SV Project 8. On the second attempt with the V8-powered brute, he lapped the 20.8-km circuit in 7 minutes and 23 seconds.
